question:
Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) totally fun first (i.e., Entertainment game reappropriated), 
        (2) mostly fun first (i.e., design workshop with disabled stakeholders),
        (3) both fun and utility first (i.e., design workshop with diverse stakeholders), 
        (4) mostly utility first (i.e., primary utilitarian mechanic designed first),
        (5) totally utility first (i.e., made by clinicians or specialists, fun incorporated later)
reasoning: The system (E-Scape) is a bespoke, accessibility-focused composition environment created by the Drake Music Project and university researchers to enable disabled people to compose and perform music independently. The design emphasizes reducing operational complexity, providing flexible control interfaces, and structuring compositional tasks into Activities to support learning and independent use. It is framed as solving utilitarian accessibility and usability problems in existing composition software, with motivation and enjoyment considered but clearly secondary to enabling functional, professional-standard composition access. There is no indication it was a repurposed entertainment game, nor that it was co-designed in a fun-first workshop with diverse or disabled stakeholders; instead it appears as a specialist, utility-driven system later evaluated with users. This aligns best with a mostly utility-first design where primary utilitarian mechanics and accessibility features are designed first, with fun and motivation incorporated but not leading the design.

question:
Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) unstructured play (i.e., no rules, making art),
        (2) semi-structured play (i.e., playground activities),
        (3) flexible structure with rules (i.e., improv),
        (4) flexible game (i.e., board game with house rules),
        (5) game with rigid rules (i.e., video game)
reasoning: The E-Scape system uses structured 'Activities' that guide users through compositional processes via menus, questions, and constrained options, but still allow creative freedom, branching, and user modification. This is a flexible structure with explicit rules and pathways rather than free play or a rigid, fixed-rule game, matching category (3) flexible structure with rules.

question:
Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely skill-based (i.e., trivia, sports),
        (2) mostly skill-based (i.e., mario kart),
        (3) equally skill and chance-based (i.e., catan),
        (4) mostly chance-based (i.e., Uno),
        (5) entirely chance-based (i.e., all dice)
reasoning: The activity is music composition using software where users make explicit compositional decisions (e.g., choosing operations, sounds, note durations, navigating branches). Outcomes are determined by user choices and skills, with no mention of randomization or chance mechanics. This aligns with an entirely skill-based task.

question:
Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely solo (i.e., solitaire),
        (2) mostly solo (i.e., playing against AI in single-player StarCraft),
        (3) mix of solo and social affordances (i.e., animal crossing),
        (4) mostly social, but aspects are independent (i.e., house on hill haunt transition),
        (5) entirely social (i.e., tag)
reasoning: The system (E-Scape) is described as software to enable disabled individuals to compose and perform music independently, with emphasis on unaided, individual use and single-user control interfaces. There is mention of group performance in other DMP software, but the study and evaluation here focus on individual composition and unaided music making, with no social or multi-user game-like interaction described. Thus the design is best characterized as entirely solo.

question:
Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely turn-based (i.e., tic tac toe),
        (2) follows a set of steps (i.e., viticulture's dynamic turn ordering),
        (3) turns are taken, but some actions can be taken at any time (i.e., pandemic),
        (4) most actions can be taken at any time, but there are some phases (i.e., PvP death reset timer),
        (5) entirely simultaneous (i.e., race)
reasoning: The E-Scape system structures compositional work as guided 'Activities' that explicitly lead the user through a series of questions and choices that build into a series of actions, often in order, with branching, repetitions, and jumps. This is described as stepping through component actions and menus, matching a design that follows a set of steps rather than free simultaneous action or purely turn-based interaction.

question:
Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely synchronous (i.e., real time strategy game),
        (2) mostly synchronous with a few asynchronous affordances (i.e., league of legends),
        (3) equal mix of synchronous and asynchronous affordances (i.e., helldivers 2),
        (4) mostly asynchronous with few synchronous affordances (i.e. cookie clicker),
        (5) entirely asynchronous (i.e., chess by postage mail)
reasoning: The system (E-Scape, Cubase, etc.) is a music composition/sequencing environment where users enter, edit, and arrange notes and then play back the result. Interaction is menu- and switch-based, focused on constructing sequences rather than continuous real-time coordination with others. While playback is in real time, the core user actions (selecting pitches, durations, copying, loading from library) are discrete and can proceed with little continuous interaction, matching an essentially asynchronous design rather than synchronous real-time gameplay.

question:
Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely competitive (i.e., spit card game),
        (2) mostly competitive, but sometimes collaboration is important (i.e., forbidden island),
        (3) mix of competitive and collaborative (i.e., mario party 2 vs 2 mini-games),
        (4) mostly collaborative (i.e., animal crossing),
        (5) entirely collaborative (i.e., pandemic)
reasoning: The system and study focus on enabling disabled individuals to compose and perform music, emphasizing individual composition, education, and accessibility. There is mention of group performance but no indication of competition, scoring, or adversarial goals. All described activities are cooperative/individual creative tasks, so the design is best characterized as entirely collaborative.

question:
Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely symmetrical (i.e., tic tac toe),
        (2) mostly symmetrical (i.e., undertale's differing NPC behaviors based on previous playthroughs),
        (3) both symmetrical and asymmetrical (i.e., pandemic with its similar turn structure but different character abilities),
        (4) mostly asymmetrical (i.e., tag),
        (5) entirely asymmetrical (i.e., keep talking, nobody explodes)
reasoning: This is not a multiplayer or adversarial game but a single-user composition environment (E-Scape) with highly customizable, user-specific interfaces (single switch, multiple switches, MIDI, mouse, etc.). There is no notion of symmetric roles between players; instead, the system is tailored asymmetrically to each user’s abilities and control methods. That best matches an entirely asymmetrical design in terms of interaction structure.
